title: Torsion en cohomologie cristalline : notes manuscrites (s.d.), copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Section 8 sets out a heuristic programme. The aim is to estimate how many Frobenius eigenvalues on the vanishing (évanescente) part of the middle cohomology of a hyperplane section are p-adic units, i.e. the slope-0 or 'ordinary' part of the vanishing cohomology.

Setting. X is smooth and proper over a perfect field k of characteristic p>0, and W=W(k). Write H(X) for crystalline cohomology taken as a complex (in modern terms RΓ_crys(X/W)).

(8.1.1) RΓ_dR(X/k) ≅ RΓ_crys(X/W) ⊗^L_W k, in D(k).

(8.1.2) This gives the universal-coefficient sequences 0→H^i(X)⊗k→H^i_dR(X)→Tor_1^W(H^{i+1}(X),k)→0. They are functorial in X. Grothendieck notes this already works for p≠2 'grâce à Berthelot', which dates the typescript to roughly 1966–70 rather than 1958.

Pencil annotation (using 8.4.3 from the previous page). Take Frobenius-semisimple parts. Since Frobenius mod p on H_dR factors through H^i(X,O_X), this gives 0→(H^i(X)⊗k)_ss→H^i(X,O_X)_ss→(_pTors^{i+1}(X))_ss→0. The last term is 0 for i≥n because F is nilpotent there (slopes ≥1). The left margin gives the dual statement for V=σ^{-1}F_* (Cartier side, H(Ω)), with 'ss' as an exponent rather than an index.

Modern reading:
- H^i(O_X)_ss ≅ H^i_et(X,Z/p)⊗k (Artin–Schreier).
- The unit-root part of H^i_crys corresponds to H^i_et(X,Z_p)⊗W.
- So the sequence is the étale Z_p universal-coefficient sequence 0→H^i(Z_p)/p→H^i(Z/p)→H^{i+1}(Z_p)[p]→0, seen inside coherent and crystalline cohomology.

Hyperplane sections. Let X⊂P^r be connected of dimension n and Y a hyperplane section. Set E(Y)=Coker(H^{n-1}(X)→H^{n-1}(Y)) (crystalline) and E_dR(Y) the analogous de Rham cokernel. Restriction gives a map u=(u0,u1,u2) between the sequences (8.1.2) for i=n-1. The snake lemma gives (8.1.3):

0→Ker u0→Ker u1→Ker u2→E(Y)⊗k→E_dR(Y)→Coker u2→0,

with u2: Tor_1(H^n(X),k)→Tor_1(H^n(Y),k).

The crossed-out 8.2 identifies Tor_1(-,k)=Hom_W(k,-) (the p-torsion). It then uses Poincaré duality for torsion: Tors H^i is dual to Tors H^{2d+1-i}. On the next page this makes u2 the transpose of the Gysin map Tors^{n-1}(Y)⊗k→Tors^{n+1}(X)⊗k. A margin remark laments ('malheureusement') that Poincaré duality is not yet available; Berthelot proved it in 1974.

On the next page, two further steps follow:
- Weak Lefschetz (assumed crystalline-ly) makes E(Y) torsion-free.
- u2 is then dual to cup product with the polarisation, Tors^{n-1}(X)⊗k→Tors^{n+1}(X)⊗k, which is independent of Y.

So the discrepancy between rank E(Y) and the de Rham/Hodge count is controlled by torsion of X alone. Unit-root eigenvalues on E(Y) can then be counted through Frobenius-semisimple parts of H^{n-1}(Y,O_Y) corrected by X-terms.
errors: Notation slip: in (8.1.3) u0 denotes the reduction u0⊗k: H^{n-1}(X)⊗k→H^{n-1}(Y)⊗k. Yet E(Y) is defined with the W-level u0. Ker u0 must be read mod p, or the sequence is misstated. The snake lemma itself is applied correctly: Coker(u0⊗k)=E(Y)⊗k by right exactness.
In the annotated semisimple sequence, 'nul si i≥n' can only apply to the third term (_pTors^{i+1})_ss, which has slopes ≥1. H^n(X,O_X)_ss is generally nonzero.

The whole argument is explicitly heuristic. It relies on (i) crystalline Poincaré duality including torsion and (ii) a crystalline weak Lefschetz with torsion-free cokernel, neither available at the time. Weak Lefschetz for crystalline cohomology with integral/torsion control is delicate and not automatic.
The dating: the archive's '[à partir de 1958]' is misleading. The reference to Berthelot and p≠2 places the text around 1966–70.

ideas.what: De Rham cohomology as derived reduction mod p of crystalline cohomology, with universal-coefficient sequences
ideas.modern_name: RΓ_dR = RΓ_crys ⊗^L_W k; universal coefficient theorem
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés, 1968)

ideas.what: Frobenius-semisimple part of H^i(X,O_X) equals the semisimple part of H^i_crys⊗k, extended by (_pTors^{i+1})_ss; dual version with V/Cartier on top forms
ideas.modern_name: Unit-root (slope 0) part of crystalline cohomology vs étale Z_p and Z/p cohomology; Hasse–Witt/Cartier duality

ideas.what: Snake-lemma comparison of crystalline and de Rham vanishing cohomology of a hyperplane section, with torsion error terms
ideas.modern_name: Vanishing cohomology in crystalline setting; weak Lefschetz with torsion
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure (SGA7 for ℓ-adic vanishing cycles: Deligne–Katz)

ideas.what: Torsion Poincaré duality (Tors H^i dual to Tors H^{2d+1-i}) and the Gysin/Lefschetz map on torsion
ideas.modern_name: Crystalline Poincaré duality with torsion pairing
ideas.usually_credited_to: Berthelot (1974), Ekedahl (1980s, duality for de Rham–Witt)

ideas.what: Goal: count p-adic unit Frobenius eigenvalues on vanishing cohomology of hyperplane sections
ideas.modern_name: Ordinarity / p-rank of generic hyperplane sections; Newton vs Hodge polygon
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mazur (1972), Deligne and Illusie ('Ordinarité des intersections complètes générales', 1990)

missed.claim: Grothendieck relates the number of unit-root Frobenius eigenvalues on vanishing cohomology to p-torsion of crystalline cohomology of the ambient X. He does this through a Y-independent Lefschetz-type map on torsion (Tors^{n-1}→Tors^{n+1}, cup with the polarisation). Discussions of generic ordinarity (Illusie 1990) do not phrase the defect from ordinarity in terms of a 'torsion hard-Lefschetz' map for X.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is an early, pre-de Rham–Witt formulation of how crystalline torsion obstructs the Hodge-theoretic count of unit roots. It also suggests studying Lefschetz maps on crystalline torsion, a topic only lightly explored (cf. integral p-adic Hodge theory / Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze torsion comparisons).

missed.claim: The heuristic estimate is left resting on unproved crystalline weak Lefschetz (torsion-free cokernel) and torsion Poincaré duality. Grothendieck notes 'malheureusement' that duality is missing. The intended final count formula is not reached on this page.
missed.quote: il n'y a malheureusement ... la dualité de Poincaré
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Weak Lefschetz for integral crystalline or prismatic cohomology with torsion control is still a subtle question. The page records Grothendieck's precise expectation.

deep.surprise_reason: Most ingredients are standard: universal coefficients, the snake lemma, and the unit-root/étale comparison later done by Bloch–Illusie. The notable unpublished detail is the late-1960s programme to count unit-root eigenvalues on vanishing cohomology via crystalline torsion and a Y-independent torsion Lefschetz map. This anticipates generic-ordinarity questions; it is interesting but a heuristic sketch.
transcription_corrections: Title word is 'estimation' (typed 'eiÉonation', corrected in pencil).
The pencil insertion after 'corps parfait k' reads 'de car. p>0'.

In the bracketed annotation, '(nul si i≥n)' appears once under the middle and once under the third term. It likely applies to the third term (_pTors^{i+1})_ss, so the double occurrence in the transcription may be a duplication.
In the left margin, 'ss' as index means semisimple part for F_X=F_X^*, and 'ss' as exponent means for V_X=σ^{-1}F_{X*}. The middle term reads H^i(X,Ω^n_X) or H^0(X,Ω^n_X) (top forms) rather than Ω^·.
The bottom-left margin probably reads 'il n'y a malheureusement [pas encore?] ... la dualité de Poincaré'.
In (8.1.3), the pencil reads 'Coker u_1' under E_DR(Y) (i.e. E_DR(Y)=Coker u_1). The snake prefix '0→Ker u0→Ker u1→' is written above the line.
